extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, HUD program administrators, regulated entities, and those tracking HUD rulemaking and information-collection notices
extracted.subtask_description: An index/listing of recent Department of Housing and Urban Development Federal Register documents (notices, proposed rules, rules) that identify public-comment opportunities, statutory authorities, SORN changes, and other procedural actions. Useful for finding open comment periods, PRA notices, and HUD regulatory actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act: OMB approval and public comment solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD is seeking approval from the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for the information collection described below. In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act, HUD is requesting comments from all interested parties on the proposed collection of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notices explicitly request public comment and OMB approval for information collections; they specify comment periods (commonly 30 or 60 days). When preparing comments on PRA notices, commenters should address the information collection's necessity, burden estimates, proposed forms/instruments, and ways to minimize respondent burden. The page includes multiple instances of 30-day and 60-day PRA notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified public comment period lengths (30-day and 60-day notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this notice is to allow for 60 days of public comment. (Other entries indicate 30 days of public comment.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different PRA notices set different statutory comment windows (commonly 30 or 60 days). Submit comments within the stated window; supplemental or separate reopenings may provide additional opportunities. Be explicit about which docket/collection your comment addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental notices can re-open or re-open public comment for specified topics
rubrics_metrics.description: This supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking re-opens public comment for certain topics and provisions that were addressed in HUD's May 29, 2024, proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental notice may reopen comment only for particular topics or provisions; comments outside the reopened scope may be treated as outside the supplemental docket. Review the supplemental notice to identify which issues are reopened and tailor comments to those topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB/information-collection notices should identify the information requested and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD is seeking approval from the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for the information collection described below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRA notices must describe the proposed collection, its purpose, and how the information will be used. Effective comments evaluate clarity of the collection, whether questions are necessary, and suggest specific changes to reduce burden or improve utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act SORN modifications require public notice with Supplementary Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the provisions of the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended, the Department of the Housing and Urban Development (HUD) is issuing public notice of its intent to modify the system of records for [system name]. The updates made are explained in the 'Supplementary Section' of this notice. This notice supersedes the previously published SORN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When HUD modifies a System of Records, it publishes a SORN notice that identifies changes and includes a Supplementary Information section explaining modifications, new routine uses, and changes to system managers. Comments should target proposed routine uses, privacy impacts, and clarity of the Supplementary Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency response or follow-up documents may summarize or respond to received comments
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice updates the FY 2026 FMRs for seven areas based on new survey data. Further, HUD responds to comments received on the FY 2026 FMRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent notices or final actions may incorporate survey data and include HUD's responses to previously submitted public comments. Commenters can expect agencies to address significant issues raised and to explain data-driven changes; tracking docket history helps evaluate whether comments influenced outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays, rescissions, or removals of previously published rules are published with explanatory notice
rubrics_metrics.description: This publication announces that HUD is delaying the effective date of HUD's January 6, 2025, final rule for all provisions not currently in effect, until the publication of an additional final rule. / This document announces the immediate rescission of the 'Final Determination...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies publish formal notices when delaying effective dates, rescinding prior determinations, or removing obsolete regulations. Such notices explain the legal basis and scope of the change; stakeholders should monitor these notices for changes affecting compliance timelines or programmatic responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory-authority based notices must cite the governing statute and describe statutory effects
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with Section 206A of the National Housing Act, HUD is providing notice of adjustment to the Basic Statutory Mortgage Limits for Multifamily Housing Programs for Calendar Year 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices that implement statutory adjustments cite the enabling law and explain how statutory formulas or indices are applied. Comments should reference the statutory framework if challenging methodology or requesting alternative interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking notices may include policy rationales and proposed regulatory text affecting stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule would harmonize HUD's existing Equal Access regulations with the directions of the Executive Order titled 'Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government.' The rule would remove references to 'gender' and 'gender identity' ... and would also provide grant recipients ... the ability to require reasonable assurances and evidence to confirm the sex of an individual seeking service...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed rules contain background, rationale, and proposed regulatory changes; commenters should address substantive legal and practical impacts, provide evidence or data, and, if appropriate, propose alternative regulatory language. Pay attention to how proposed changes affect covered parties (grantees, owners, operators, managers) and operational practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices removing obsolete regulations must identify replacements or consolidation history
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule removes HUD's Shelter Plus Care program and Supportive Housing Program regulations from title 24 of the Code of Federal Regulations. HUD is removing these regulations and references to these regulations because the Shelter Plus Care and Supportive Housing Programs were consolidated into and replaced by the Continuum of Care (CoC) Program following the enactment of the Homeless Emergency Assistance and Rapid Transition to Housing Act of 2009 (HEARTH Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal notices explain why regulations are obsolete (e.g., consolidation, statutory changes) and identify where governing authorities now reside. Comments can request clarifications about cross-references, transitional responsibilities, or residual obligations arising from the removed rules.
